line: Crowley’s Four of Disks: Power, Chesed establishing the Universe in three dimensions, the Sun in Capricorn.

sections.title: What Crowley names
sections.line: The chapter name for the card. The second quotation gives the element of its suit.

sections.title: Its place on the Tree and in the zodiac
sections.line: The Four, Chesed, shows the Universe established in three dimensions below the Abyss. The card is ruled by the Sun in Capricorn.

quotes.quote: The Four, Chesed, shows the establishment of the Universe in three dimensions, that is, below the Abyss.
These cards are attributed to Chesed.
The card is ruled by the Sun in Capricornus

sections.title: What it figures
sections.line: Crowley reads the card as Law and Order, and the disks as a fortress whose defence is valid only when violently active.

quotes.quote: This represents Law and Order, maintained by constant authority and vigilance.
The disks themselves are square; revolution is very opposite to the card; and they contain the signs of the Four Elements.
